payload.statement_nl: Let f : ℤ → ℝ → ℝ and g : ℤ → ℤ → ℝ be fixed families of real-valued functions. For every integer n with n > 1, every integer k with 0 ≤ k ≤ n - 1, and every real number t with k ≤ n*t < k + 1, one has f(n)(t) ≤ g(n)(k).

result_payload.candidate_counterexample: Take f(n)(t)=1 for all n and t, and g(n)(k)=0 for all n and k. Then for any admissible n>1, k, and t with k <= n*t < k+1, the conclusion becomes 1 <= 0, a contradiction.

detailed_findings.finding: The statement has no hypotheses relating f and g, so it is not valid in this level of generality.
A concrete counterexample is given by constant functions f=1 and g=0, which violates the claimed inequality for every admissible triple (n,k,t).
No proof text is provided, so there is no derivation to check even before addressing falsity.
